_comment: Copy to config/crew-dispatch.json (gitignored, local) to activate. The FIRST MATE (you, the supervisor) reads these rules and picks the best-fit profile with judgment, then passes concrete --model/--effort flags to fm-spawn.sh. The shell scripts DO NOT parse these rules — they only enforce that when this file exists, a ship/scout dispatch must carry an explicit --model (the consultation backstop, so the rules are never silently skipped). A per-task captain override ('use haiku for this') always wins over the rules. Claude models launch on the Superset custom agent labeled Claude; gpt-*/codex-* models launch on the agent labeled Codex. An omitted model/effort means the instance default is used (no flag). Write bare model IDs here — superset-launch appends the [1m] suffix to configured 1M-capable Claude models; an explicit bracket suffix is respected as-is, and other model IDs are untouched.

rules.when: The task is a trivial mechanical edit — a rote rename, formatting sweep, targeted typo fix, dependency bump, or simple file gathering.
rules.why: Cheapest fast profile when the task is narrow and low-ambiguity.

rules.when: The task is a focused, well-scoped bug fix or a small single-file feature with clear acceptance criteria.
rules.why: Mid profile: capable enough for real code, cheaper than Opus for bounded work.

rules.when: The task is a big or ambiguous multi-file feature, a risky refactor, a subtle concurrency/perf bug, or work that requires holding many moving parts in mind.
rules.why: Strongest profile for broad design and hard implementation work.

rules.when: A read-only scout / investigation that just has to read code and report — no edits, no risk.
rules.why: Scouts are throwaway and don't ship; a cheap model reads and summarizes fine.
